title: Mixed Blessing: Class-Wise Embedding guided Instance-Dependent Partial Label Learning

problem.claim: Instance-dependent noisy labels create a partial-label learning setting in which candidate labels are related to sample features and difficult to distinguish from the ground-truth label.

gap.claim: Conventional partial-label learning assumes instance-independent noise and does not directly address the feature-dependent ambiguity of practical noisy labels.

contributions.claim: The method constructs class-wise embeddings for each sample to model relationships among candidate and non-candidate labels in instance-dependent partial-label learning.
The method uses class prototypes carrying global feature information to disambiguate candidate labels.
A public code implementation is provided.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present the creation of class-wise embeddings for each sample as a first-time contribution for this problem.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive comparisons against twelve methods across six benchmark datasets, including four fine-grained datasets.
The authors report that these experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

narrative_sequence.summary: Partial-label learning represents each sample with a candidate label set containing the true label and noisy alternatives.
Practical noisy labels depend on sample features, producing instance-dependent partial-label learning and substantial ambiguity.
The approach models candidate-label relationships with class-wise embeddings and reduces ambiguity with global class prototypes.
The authors evaluate the approach against twelve methods on six benchmark datasets and report effectiveness.

source_observation.claim: Feature-dependent noisy labels can contain useful sample information while also increasing ambiguity between candidate and true labels.

interpretation.claim: Noise should be modeled as potentially informative structure rather than treated only as an obstacle.

application.claim: In related weak-supervision settings, represent label relationships and global class information jointly when ambiguity is feature-dependent.

exception.claim: This lesson may not transfer when label noise is independent of instance features or when class-level global information is unavailable.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the model architecture, optimization procedure, or loss functions.
The abstract does not provide quantitative results or dataset names.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported effectiveness.
